title: Would you play games that were made with no human in the loop?
author: Dredgefort
selftext:
I don't think we're that far off to be honest. 

A model comes up with a concept, executes/iterates on that concept, and produces a 'finished' product then ships it to steam or some other platform. I'll be suprised if someone hasn't already attempted this. 

Would the fact that no human was in the loop what-so-ever bother you?

comments.author: Brief_Shopping2222
comments.body: I only play heroes of might and magic 3 so this wouldn't effect me either way

replies.author: Galitzianer0
replies.body: "AI, please come up with the game Heroes of Might and Magic 3, make no mistakes"

comments.author: NullKalahar
comments.body:
Todo jogo tem intervenção humana, a ia não faz nada se não for solicitado.

Eu jogaria um jogo feito por ia sem problemas

replies.author: Dredgefort
replies.body: The basic prompt could be "Make games with unique and interesting gameplay, do research to find gameplay that's fun and engaging. Make the graphics and audio look highly polished, keep iterating until perfect. Once you're done and happy with it, publish it to steam", stick it in a loop and you're done.

replies.author: Kopteeni
replies.body: You forgot the most important part of the prompt: make no mistakes

replies.author: Antiox123456
replies.body: Try it and you'll see it'll create the most generic AI slop there is.

comments.author: Every-Prize4720
comments.body: if the game is good it doesnt matter how much ai was used. making good game is hard for now atleast.

comments.author: __Arkos__
comments.body:
Matters not if the game is good. Having a human in the loop doesn't necessarily make it a good product. The quadruple-A landscape has shown that time and time again. But this too is equally true for the opposite, keep that in mind as well. 

We'll just have to wait and see how it all plays out.

comments.author: wewerecreaturres
comments.body: No because they won’t be any good

comments.author: Arbejdstilsynet
comments.body: If the game is good, I don't give a shit and neither would a lot of people.

comments.author: Eseatease
comments.body: Sure why not

replies.author: Dredgefort
replies.body: Would you pay a normal indie price for it? I.e. $5 - $20? Curious if the fact it's completely machine generated would effect how people value something.

replies.author: Eseatease
replies.body: If it's the same quality ofc, I haven't noticed or cared how games were made in the past nor do i today. Either it's good or not.

comments.author: akanas
comments.body: Guys, stop dreaming of creating a low effort game that will be good. AI certainly gives us the tools to ship faster, but AI can't understand what is fun and how everything feels. You need to constantly iterate over the aspects of the game that supposed to be fun. A probabilistic text generator can't know what is fun.

replies.author: redditscraperbot2
replies.body: I feel like the latest model releases have created a situation where it's technically possible to create something you could call a game and it has attracted the wrong crowd. A good game still needs QA, testing, manual adjustments and most of all a plan. We are about to see a glut of three.js roguelites so it's basically rip for that genre.

comments.author: Affectionate_Fact854
comments.body:
I think no human in the loop games is quite a big statement to make unless you are just directly cloning minecraft or gta...

I spent the last month and a half doing various different orchestration.md methods to automate the process 

Key finding was when I let it completely automate with design documents and goal documents without having phased stops where human input is required , the game starts drifting and becoming slop 


To make the game still end up being fun and make sense you still need those phase stops in order to guide the ai back on track and to tell it where it needs to make adjustments before it moves on to more implementations 


If you don't,  the project just simply becomes a big mess, that even the ai eventually gets confused with that in turn leads to even more unnecessary token burn 


So in a nutshell I have no expectations for a game with 0 human iteration

replies.author: Blueberry_Gecko
replies.body: Even if you clone minecraft, pretty sure that had a human in the loop :P

replies.author: Affectionate_Fact854
replies.body:
Yes yes smarty pants obviously there is a initial human interaction in the loop 

But it doesn't change the point of human iteration is needed  to polish a game to the point that its worth sharing :P

comments.author: Opelmannator
comments.body: I allready play.

comments.author: heavy-minium
comments.body:
>I don't think we're that far off to be honest.

But we are far off that! Let's forget about AI for a moment and think of all those big companies that have vast resources at their disposal, and yet still publish games that have lots of negative reviews. AI solves a narrow problem, which is the problem of having enough development resources, but the main challenge of creating a game that is fun is still largely unsolved.

comments.author: Victorex123
comments.body: I play games because I like to empathize with the author, if there is no author. There is a problem. 🤔

comments.author: RevenantLadder
comments.body: Considering the industry is plagued with activists larping as game devs nowadays I'd be open to it, yeah.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body: Who cares

comments.author: YKLKTMA
comments.body: Forget the idea that you can create anything even remotely good with an LLM without using your brain. All you’ll end up with is a pile of slop that almost nobody will want to play, let alone pay for.

comments.author: Dignified_Cyclops
comments.body: NGL, customers don't care about what's under the hood. They just want a game (for what ever reasons they want it).

comments.author: daddywookie
comments.body:
Me personally? No, but then I don't play the kind of games that this workflow would generate.

However, there is a huge market for hyper-casual ad supported games. Pick up the phone of any bored mother at school pickup and you'll see a lot of games you have never heard of that offer 30 minutes of distraction.

I could easily see an almost entirely AI studio with a closed loop to evaluate which monetisation and retention tactics work best and then using this to churn out a steady stream of "new" hyper-casual games. There is little thought in the production because there is little thought in the consumption. It's all about volume.

This kind of games development is pretty soulless anyway, you are literally building an attention gambling machine with plenty of dark patterns. I'm sure the money men would love to cut out those pesky designers and developers with their artistic dreams and moral consciences.

comments.author: ByteFoundry
comments.body:
I am doing the same tests at the moment and see the same thing. Without a human who directs the flow the models tend to find unnecessary work or tangents and start to focus on them. Drifting describes it well.

A human needs to be the product owner and act like it.

comments.author: IUsedToMakeMaps
comments.body:
All things being equal? No. My time is limited and there are already a billion game choices in front of me. Why would I choose the one with the lowest effort? 

But all things aren't equal and I highly doubt your no-human-in-the-loop game would in any way be considered "good", and therefore would never be in contention for my money, except possibly as a novelty ("let's see what this trainwreck looks like").

comments.author: Nico1300
comments.body: No, I don't thin any of these games will be fun, we've got plenty of ai games with a human in loop and most of them are either bad or just a tech demo ripoff of a popular game.

comments.author: tabaxi_gf
comments.body: We’re not there yet but when it’s fun enough I and most people would consider it

comments.author: Blueberry_Gecko
comments.body: Riddle me this: If *you* don't care about your game, why would I care?

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
No. Though it would make the game uncopyrightable, so you wouldn't be able to make money from it.

That being said, I'm very picky with games. And I have a feeling even with enough advancement in the field (which is going to be bottlenecked by hardware at some point due to chip materials being finite and datacenters burning through them until they figure out some new way to build the architecture), and compute and time, you might end up with, say, Cyberpunk as it was when it first released. You know, missing that 20% that takes us 95% of the time to build. But a 10/10 game missing 20% isn't a 8/10. It's a 4/10. Which is well below my threshold of giving a fuck. So I doubt I'd find it fun or play it even if you could make a sick trailer from it and wow the pants off a Tik Tok audience.
